report:
Conclusion: the difference looks like a shift toward web/blog/ad-style tokens — i.e., B (minus A) pushes the residual stream in a direction that increases logits for tokens common in informal web/news/blogging and advertising content.

Why I conclude that
- The highest-norm cells’ logit-lens top tokens are dominated by blog/news/ad vocabulary: “blog”, “blogs”, “blogger”, “blogging”, “photo”, “facebook”, “ad”, “ads”, “Mail”, “TV”, “seminar”, “Money/revenue/purchases”, “sexy”, and punctuation/newline/parenthesis tokens often used in list/ad formatting.
- There are also many named-entity / newsy tokens (Obama, billionaire, politicians, activists, journalists, chairman) which are typical of news/social-media copy.
- The difference is concentrated at early token positions and middle→late layers (strong norms around layers ~16–25, especially pos0–pos2), consistent with a change that affects content selection at the start of generation (i.e., steering toward particular topical/genre tokens).

Caveats
- Patchscope continuations were not provided here, so I can’t show actual generation-level behavior; the claim is based on logit-lens directions and norm concentration only.
- This evidence supports saying the models differ in their tendency to favor web/blog/advertising vocabulary, but it doesn’t prove the exact training cause (e.g., additional web/blog data, an ad-oriented fine-tune, or some tokenizer/positioning effect).
